title: Selling a car you are still paying off
text: You can sell us a car you still owe money on. While the loan is open, your lender (the lienholder) holds the title, or the electronic title record, so you don't need the title in hand, and you don't need a duplicate if you can't find it. At the appointment we confirm what you owe and pay the lender off directly from your offer. If the offer is more than the payoff, you get the difference ([When and how you get paid](kb:getting_paid)). If it's less, see [If you owe more than our offer](kb:negative_equity). To speed things up, get a [payoff letter](kb:payoff_letter) before you come in.

title: Getting a payoff letter from your lender
text: A payoff letter is a document from your lender that states exactly how much it takes to close your loan. Most lenders let you download one from your online account, or you can call them. It must show your account number, the payoff amount, the date it is good through, and where to send payment. Ask for a 10-day payoff amount, because daily interest changes the total. Bring it to your appraisal appointment ([What to bring](kb:appointment_checklist)).

title: Getting a payoff letter from your lender
text: A payoff letter is a document from your lender that states exactly how much it takes to close your loan. Download it from your lender's website or call them. It must show your account number, the payoff amount, the date it is good through, and where to send payment. Ask for a 15-day payoff amount, because daily interest changes the total. Don't want to call your lender? Sign the lender payoff authorization, form NW-LPA-1, and we request the letter for you; allow 2 business days. NW-LPA-1 is for loans only; for a lease, see [Selling a car that you lease](kb:leased_car) and form NW-LSE-1. If your lender is in our [e-payoff network](kb:epayoff_network), you don't need a letter at all.

title: Lenders in our e-payoff network
text: Lenders in our e-payoff network share payoff amounts with us electronically. If your loan is with one of them, you don't need a payoff letter: we confirm the payoff directly with the lender the same day, at your appointment, using your loan account number. Network lenders: Bayline Credit Union, Northwind Auto Finance, Meridian Auto Loans, Pinewood Federal Credit Union and Lakeshore Bank. Granite Bank joins the network on March 15, 2026. For any other lender, bring a [payoff letter](kb:payoff_letter) or sign NW-LPA-1 so we can request one.

title: If you owe more than our offer
text: Sometimes the amount left on a loan is higher than our offer. This is called negative equity, or being upside down. You can still sell us the car, but you pay the difference at the appointment, after we compare the offer with your [payoff letter](kb:payoff_letter). We accept a cashier's check, a debit card or a personal check for this payment. We can't accept credit cards.

title: If you owe more than our offer
text: Sometimes the amount left on a loan is higher than our offer. This is called negative equity, or being upside down. You can still sell us the car, but you pay the difference at the appointment, after we compare the offer with your [payoff letter](kb:payoff_letter). We accept a cashier's check or a debit card. We no longer accept personal checks, and we do not accept credit cards. If you'd rather not pay the difference, you can keep the car: an offer never obliges you to sell.

title: When and how you get paid
text: Once the paperwork is signed, we pay you by bank draft at the store, by direct deposit (1 to 3 business days), or by a check mailed to your address (5 to 7 business days). If there's a loan on the car, we send the payoff to your lender within 2 business days, and you receive the amount left over. Keep making your loan payments until your lender confirms the payoff ([Should I keep making loan payments?](kb:keep_paying_until_confirmed)).

title: When and how you get paid
text: Once the paperwork is signed, we pay you by bank draft or by direct deposit, which arrives in 1 to 3 business days. We no longer mail checks. If you used [home pickup](kb:home_pickup), the $99 fee is taken out of your payment. If there's a loan, we send the payoff to your lender within 2 business days, or the same day for lenders in our [e-payoff network](kb:epayoff_network), and you receive the amount left over. Keep making payments until your lender confirms the payoff ([Should I keep making loan payments?](kb:keep_paying_until_confirmed)). An extra payment comes back from your lender ([Getting back an extra loan payment](kb:lender_overpayment_refund)).

title: Should I keep making loan payments?
text: Yes. Keep making your regular loan payments until your lender confirms that the loan is paid off. Our payoff covers the amount the lender quoted, and a missed payment in the meantime can be reported as late on your credit history. If a payment goes through after the payoff, your lender refunds it to you ([Getting back an extra loan payment](kb:lender_overpayment_refund)).

title: Getting back an extra loan payment
text: If your lender receives both our payoff and one of your regular payments, the extra amount belongs to you. Your lender refunds it directly to you, usually within 2 to 4 weeks after the loan is closed. Northwind doesn't receive or forward overpayments, so contact your lender if the refund doesn't arrive.

title: My loan is paid off but the lien is still on the title
text: If you've paid off your loan but the title still lists the lender as lienholder, the lien hasn't been released yet. Ask your lender for a lien release letter. If you can't get one, sign the lien release request, form NW-LRL-1, and we contact the lender for you; this can add 1 to 2 weeks. We can still make an offer and book your appointment while you wait. In states with [electronic titles](kb:electronic_titles), the lender sends the release to the state electronically.
